messages:
secops: :rotating_light: Urgent: External vendor received a support bundle that appears to contain plaintext OAuth tokens and one env file with service credentials. Treat as high severity — assume tokens are compromised and rotate immediately.

maya (support): Confirmed. Bundle id=sb-2026-03-23-77 was uploaded to vendor-support/redwood/ on 2026-03-23 10:12. It included debug.log and .env.backup. I pulled the bundle and redacted what I could, but vendor may have already downloaded. We notified them and asked to delete.

toni (infra): Any idea how .env.backup left the support bundle? Our support tool should scrub dotfiles by default.

leo (dev): Looks like the support dump script picks everything under /app/runtime for convenience. There was an edge case: build-time copies of env files get saved as .env.backup in /app/runtime/tmp when a migration fails. Support script didn't exclude tmp.

sam (oncall): Quick detection commands for teams to run across workspaces and S3:

```
# find potential oauth tokens in artifacts
rg --no-ignore --hidden "(xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-_]{24,}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9_]{36,}|ya29\.[0-9A-Za-z-_\.]+)" -S --follow --line-number || true
# list recent support bundles uploaded to vendor repo
aws s3 ls s3://vendor-support/redwood/ --recursive --human-readable --summarize | tail -n 50
```

legal-bot: If vendor access was granted under NDA, we've asked for immediate deletion and an audit of who accessed the bundle. Legal will prepare a short disclosure if required.

secops: Action items (company-wide):
- Immediate: Revoke any tokens found in the identified bundle and any tokens that match patterns in other recent bundles. Consider them compromised.
- Notify: Tell third-party vendor to confirm deletion and provide access logs. If they cannot confirm, escalate to legal.
- Patch: Update support-bundle builder to exclude tmp, dotfiles, and to run a scrubber that removes environment-like files before packaging.
- Audit: Search the last 90 days of support bundles for secrets; create a ticket tracker and list of affected tokens.
- Policy: Enforce automated pre-upload secret-scan step for all outbound support uploads. Failure blocks upload until cleared.

leo (dev): I'll open MR #7012 to change the support dump list and add a preflight scrubber. Also adding a unit test to simulate migration failures so .env.backup doesn't land in the bundle.

toni (infra): We rotated the infra-owned API keys that could have matched the pattern and added a short-lived token replacement for integrations with vendors. Also added enforcement: s3://vendor-support/redwood/ now requires requestor to be in allowlist and uploads are disabled from CI tokens.

maya (support): Vendor replied: they downloaded once, then deleted and provided a download log (user vendor-agent@partner.co). Legal is reviewing.

sam (oncall): Examples for token revocation procedures: 
```
# GitHub token rotation: create a new PAT, update services, then delete old token from web UI / API
curl -H "Authorization: token $NEW_TOKEN" https://api.github.com/user
# Slack token revocation (workspace app token)
# use admin UI or apps.admin.conversations.revoke where applicable
```

secops: Timeline: discovery -> containment -> rotation should be complete within 48 hours. Post status here when rotations and vendor confirmation are done.

legal-bot: Legal requested copies of vendor logs and initial notif text. Maya please DM me the vendor contact and the exact bundle id.

leo (dev): MR #7012 opened and pipeline test added. Scrubber includes rg-based secret removal and a denylist for file patterns (.env*, *.pem, *_key). Will roll to canary support tool in ~1h.

toni (infra): I've enabled object-level logging on the vendor bucket and created a short retention forensic hold tag 'sec-2311111111'. Will share logs when available.

secops: One more policy change: effective immediately, no outbound support uploads to external vendors are allowed unless a runbook-approved scrubber passes and the upload is authorized by Support Lead. A doc and automation will be published in 72 hours.

maya (support): Understood. We'll retrain the support team and update the runbook.

sam (oncall): Scans across the last 90 days started; will post findings to SEC-2311111111 and ping this thread for high-priority hits.

secops: Thanks all. If you find more bundles with cleartext secrets that were publicly accessible before deletion, escalate immediately to legal and AMs. Thread open for updates.
